theorem principalMinor_weighted_integral_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (S : Finset (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) (hiS : i ∈ S) (hi0 : i ≠ (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n))
    (h : ℝ → ℝ) (hh : Measurable h)
    (hL1 : Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => h ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n))) (orthogonalHaar n)) :
    Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).submatrix (Subtype.val : S → Fin n) (Subtype.val : S → Fin n)).det * h ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n))) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
      (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ, ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).submatrix (Subtype.val : S → Fin n) (Subtype.val : S → Fin n)).det * h ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n)) ∂orthogonalHaar n) = 0
sealed_proposal_signatures.signed_sqrt_det_integral:
theorem signed_sqrt_det_integral {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ)
    (h : ℝ → ℝ) (hh : Measurable h)
    (hL1 : Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => h ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n))) (orthogonalHaar n)) :
    (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det *
        h ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n)) ∂orthogonalHaar n) =
      ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (n - 1) * (Real.sqrt κ - 1) ^ (n - 1) / (2 : ℝ) ^ n) *
        (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
          ((Real.sqrt κ + 1) * ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n)) - (Real.sqrt κ - 1)) *
            h ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n) (⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩ : Fin n)) ∂orthogonalHaar n)

nodes.statement: Orthogonal O preserves Euclidean norm; fixed orthogonal left multiplication preserves full Haar law. These are background inputs used by the author, not new conclusions of B.6.

Finite-dimensional determinant multiplicativity, determinant of transpose, determinant of scalar matrix/scalar multiple, finite determinant expansion, and real finite-expectation linearity are background facts invoked by the displayed argument.
Let a=sqrt(kappa)+1 and b=sqrt(kappa)-1. Literal A_O=(1/4)(aI-bO)^T(aI-bO).
For 0<=t<=b one has a-t>=2 and b>=0, so the displayed path interval reaches t=b.
For 0<=t<=b and v in R^n, ||(aI-tO)v|| >= (a-t)||v|| >= 2||v||.
aI-tO is invertible throughout 0<=t<=b.
nodes.source_evidence: Thus ... is invertible throughout this interval.

nodes.statement: The determinant of aI-tO is positive at t=0 (a>0 and det(aI)=a^n>0).
The determinant along t in [0,b] is continuous and never zero, so remains positive; in particular det(aI-bO)>0.
nodes.source_evidence: Its determinant is positive at t=0 and remains positive by continuity.

nodes.statement: Taking determinants in Eq16 gives det A_O=2^(-2n)(det(aI-bO))^2; the positive determinant fixes the positive real square-root branch.
sqrt(det A_O)=2^(-n) det(aI-bO).
Multiply aI-bO by O^T and use OO^T=I and det(O^T)=det(O), obtaining det(O)det(aI-bO)=det(aO^T-bI).
det(O)sqrt(det A_O)=2^(-n)det(aO^T-bI). This is the first displayed equality of Eq18.
Transposing aO^T-bI preserves its determinant, giving det(aO^T-bI)=det(aO-bI).
nodes.source_evidence: the last equality follows by transposing

nodes.statement: det(O)sqrt(det A_O)=2^(-n)det(aO-bI). This is the second displayed equality of Eq18 used in the subsequent expansion.
For every S subset of {1,...,n}, O_{S,S} is the principal submatrix, with det O_{empty,empty}=1.
If S contains i>=2, set row reflection D_i=I_n-2e_i e_i^T.
D_i is orthogonal (it changes exactly one coordinate sign), so left Haar invariance applies to O -> D_i O.
D_i O has the same distribution as O under full O(n) Haar.
(D_i O)_11=O_11=U since i>=2.
det((D_i O)_{S,S})=-det(O_{S,S}) since row i is present in the principal submatrix.
For every S, |det O_{S,S}| <= 1. This exact source estimate is retained as its own node.

nodes.statement: Each scalar-weighted term in this finite expansion is integrable, hence its finite sum and 2^(-n) multiple are integrable.

E[det(O)sqrt(det A_O)h(U)]=2^(-n) sum_S a^{|S|}(-b)^{n-|S|}E[det O_{S,S}h(U)]. This is the first equality of Ex55 after the displayed left-hand side.

nodes.statement: The empty-set term is (-b)^n E[h(U)], using det(empty)=1 and |empty|=0.
The {1} term is a(-b)^(n-1) E[Uh(U)], since det O_{{1},{1}}=U and |{1}|=1. E[Uh(U)] is finite, also following from the singleton case of the minor bound.
The expectation equals 2^(-n)[(-b)^n E[h(U)]+a(-b)^(n-1)E[Uh(U)]]. This is the second equality of Ex55.
Factor (-1)^(n-1)b^(n-1), and combine the finite expectations into E[(aU-b)h(U)]. This right-hand integrand is integrable by the empty and singleton cases and finite linearity.
E[det(O)sqrt(det A_O)h(U)] = ((-1)^(n-1)(sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1)/2^n) E[((sqrt(kappa)+1)U-(sqrt(kappa)-1))h(U)].
